 Judgment
1.
Both the KSRTC as well as the claimant are in appeal challenging the judgment and award of the Tribunal on the ground of negligence as well as quantum of compensation.
2. The learned counsel for the KSRTC contends that attribution of negligence by the Tribunal solely on the driver of the KSRTC bus, is incorrect.
It was also argued that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is excessive.
3. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the claimant contends that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate in as much as the income determined by the Tribunal is incorrect.

sentences.text: 4. The contention advanced by the claimant was that the claimant was traveling in the motorcycle as a pillion rider and KSRTC bus hit the motorcycle from behind.

The Counsel for the KSRTC, however,
contended that the charge sheet produced indicate that the collision occurred when the two wheeler,
in which the claimant was traveling, came in from the side road onto the main road.

5. However, this contention is not supported by the evidence of the driver of the bus, in as much as,
the driver has denied the entire accident itself.
Thus, this argument of the learned counsel for the KSRTC, cannot be accepted.
6. It is not in dispute that the charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the bus.
It is also not in dispute that the KSRTC has not seriously disputed the accident.
However, the driver of the bus has not stated anything about the accident to prove that even the claimant was negligent in occurrence of the accident.
7. In my view, there is no evidence to indicate that there is some negligence on the rider of the motorcycle.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in coming to the conclusion that the accident occurred only due to the negligence of the driver of the bus.
Hence, the said finding of the Tribunal is confirmed.

8. As far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence,
has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered fracture of left neck of femur with morel level lesion of left thigh.
9. The doctor, who was examined has stated that the claimant has suffered disability of 20% to particular limb.

Since, the claimant has suffered fracture of femur and having regard to the opinion of the doctor, in my view, the whole body disability has to be determined at 10% instead of 6%
determined by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.6,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2015, would be Rs.9,000/-.
11.
It is the contention of the KSRTC that the claimant was aged 46 years as stated by the claimant in the claim petition.
But the Tribunal relying on the medical records i.e., wound certificate has taken the age of the claimant as 40 years and applied multiplier of 15.

In my view, since the claimant himself has stated in the claim petition that he was aged 46 years and there is no evidence to indicate his age, it would be appropriate to consider the age of the claimant as 46 years and apply correct multiplier of 13.
Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.140,400 (9000 x 12 x 13 x 10%) towards 'loss of future income' .

4 12.
Having regard to the nature of injuries, the laid up period has to be treated as 3 months instead of 2 months taken by the Tribunal.
As a consequence, the amount of Rs.12,000/- awarded by the Tribunal towards 'loss of income during the laid up period' would also stand enhanced to Rs.27,000/- (9,000 X 3 months).
13. Having regard to the injuries suffered by the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' as against Rs.25,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

14. Having regard to the lasting effects of the injuries on the claimant, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities, as against the sum of Rs.20,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

15. Having regard to the length of the stay of the claimant in the hospital, the claimant would also be entitled to 'conveyance, food and nourishment and attendant charges' at Rs.20,000/- as against the sum of Rs.15,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. The sums awarded as 'medical expenses' and 'future medical expenses' by the Tribunal, being based on documentary evidence, does not call for modification and hence confirmed.
17. Consequently the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.368,992/- as against Rs.225,517/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
19. The KSRTC is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
20. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal.
21. The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transferred to the Tribunal for disbursement.
Both the appeals are accordingly disposed of.
